title: The ‘Enemies List’ at Madison Square Garden

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Bilbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today, with little warning or regulation, more and more companies have begun using facial recognition technology on their customers, they say, as a security measure.
sentences.zh: 如今，在几乎没有预警或监管的情况下，越来越多的公司开始以“安全措施”为由，对顾客使用人脸识别技术。

sentences.en: So what happens when it's actually being used to punish a company's enemies?
sentences.zh: 那么，当这项技术被用来惩罚公司的“敌人”时，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: My colleague, Kashmir Hill, tried to find out.
sentences.zh: 我的同事克什米尔·希尔试图找出答案。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 18th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月18日，星期三。

sentences.en: So, Kashmir, tell me about this reporting that you have been doing, really, in our own backyard, just a few blocks south of where you're now sitting in Midtown Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 那么，克什米尔，跟我聊聊你一直在做的这项调查吧，它其实就发生在我们自己的后院，就在你现在所在的曼哈顿中城往南几个街区的地方。

sentences.en: So, last month, I was talking to Nicolette Landy.
sentences.zh: 上个月，我和尼科莱特·兰迪聊了聊。

sentences.en: She's 29.
sentences.zh: 她今年29岁。

sentences.en: She lives in New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 她住在新泽西州。

sentences.en: She loves going to live shows, particularly at Madison Square Garden, this iconic arena here in New York City.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢去现场看演出，特别是在纽约市这个标志性的麦迪逊广场花园。

sentences.en: She went to six shows in October alone.
sentences.zh: 仅在十月份，她就看了六场演出。

sentences.en: That is a real commitment.
sentences.zh: 这真是真爱啊。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She likes going out.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢出门活动。

sentences.en: And her boyfriend had gotten her tickets to see Mariah Carey, who has this kind of, you know, legendary Christmas show that she does every year.
sentences.zh: 她男朋友给她买了玛丽亚·凯莉演唱会的票，玛丽亚每年都会举办那种传奇般的圣诞演出。

sentences.en: The one and only.
sentences.zh: 独一无二的演出。

sentences.en: All they wanted for Christmas was Mariah Carey.
sentences.zh: 他们圣诞节唯一的愿望就是看玛丽亚·凯莉。

sentences.en: Well done.
sentences.zh: 做得好。

sentences.en: And so, they bundle up.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们穿得暖暖和和的。

sentences.en: They head to Madison Square Garden.
sentences.zh: 前往麦迪逊广场花园。

sentences.en: There's a lot of security that you kind of go through to get into a show.
sentences.zh: 进场前通常要经过很多安检环节。

sentences.en: So, they're walking through the metal detectors, and Nicolette gets pulled aside.
sentences.zh: 他们走过金属探测器时，尼科莱特被拦了下来。

sentences.en: And a security guard asks to see her ID.
sentences.zh: 一名保安要求查看她的身份证件。

sentences.en: Never a good sign.
sentences.zh: 这可不是什么好兆头。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: She hasn't presented her ticket yet or anything.
sentences.zh: 她当时还没出示门票之类的东西。

sentences.en: She doesn't really know why she's been pulled aside.
sentences.zh: 她其实不知道自己为什么被拦下。

sentences.en: But she gets out her ID, shows it to them, and this confirms her name.
sentences.zh: 但她还是拿出身份证件给他们看，这确认了她的名字。

sentences.en: And her name is on a watch list at Madison Square Garden.
sentences.zh: 而她的名字就在麦迪逊广场花园的黑名单上。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so, what does that mean for her?
sentences.zh: 那这对她意味着什么？

sentences.en: She is not allowed to go to the concert.
sentences.zh: 她不被允许进入演唱会现场。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 啊。

sentences.en: Her boyfriend can go, but she can't.
sentences.zh: 她男朋友可以进去，但她不行。

sentences.en: So, quite crushingly, she is being told, you cannot go in.
sentences.zh: 所以，非常令人沮丧的是，她被告知：你不能进去。

sentences.en: You cannot see Mariah Carey.
sentences.zh: 你不能看玛丽亚·凯莉的演出。

sentences.en: Turn around.
sentences.zh: 转头。

sentences.en: Go home.
sentences.zh: 回家吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She is turned away.
sentences.zh: 她被拒之门外了。

sentences.en: And her boyfriend didn't go either.
sentences.zh: 她男朋友最后也没进去。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Which makes him a gentleman, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想这说明他是个绅士。

sentences.en: So, how did that happen?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是怎么发生的呢？

sentences.en: So, as she walked through the metal detector, there was a camera there, and it had a facial recognition system.
sentences.zh: 当她走过金属探测器时，那里有一个摄像头，配备了人脸识别系统。

sentences.en: And so, it had scanned her face, and that is why she was pulled aside.
sentences.zh: 它扫描了她的脸，这就是她被拦下的原因。

sentences.en: And then to make sure she wasn't a doppelganger, that's why they asked for her ID to confirm that she was indeed Nicolette Landy.
sentences.zh: 为了确保她不是长得像的人，他们才要求查看身份证件，以确认她确实是尼科莱特·兰迪。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, there's a lot going on here.
sentences.zh: 这里面有很多名堂。

sentences.en: But let's first talk about the story behind this facial recognition software that's being used inside Madison Square Garden.
sentences.zh: 但我们先来谈谈麦迪逊广场花园内部所使用的人脸识别软件背后的故事。

sentences.en: So, Madison Square Garden has been using facial recognition technology going back to 2018, first used at the Grammy Awards.
sentences.zh: 麦迪逊广场花园从2018年就开始使用人脸识别技术了，最初是在格莱美颁奖典礼上使用的。

sentences.en: And it has primarily been using it to identify security threats.
sentences.zh: 它主要用于识别安全威胁。

sentences.en: So, fans who have been disorderly, who have been violent, who are essentially banned from coming in for safety reasons.
sentences.zh: 比如那些行为不端、有过暴力倾向，或者因安全原因被禁止入内的粉丝。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's how I think of facial recognition software, as being a very intense but important layer of security.
sentences.zh: 是的，我心目中的人脸识别软件就是一种非常严密但必要的安全防线。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Madison Square Garden, you know, this is in the middle of New York.
sentences.zh: 麦迪逊广场花园位于纽约市中心。

sentences.en: It's right on top of Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 就在宾夕法尼亚车站上方。

sentences.en: It is a place where you want to have good security.
sentences.zh: 那是一个你需要确保高度安全的地方。

sentences.en: It's a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 人流量非常大。

sentences.en: It's the kind of place that could be targeted.
sentences.zh: 它很容易成为目标。

sentences.en: And so, they do have pretty intense security there.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们那里的安保确实非常严密。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Which really does make sense.
sentences.zh: 这确实很有道理。

sentences.en: So, how did Nicolette fit into these security protocols at Madison Square Garden?
sentences.zh: 那么，尼科莱特是怎么被纳入麦迪逊广场花园的这些安保协议中的呢？

sentences.en: Why would she have been seen as a danger?
sentences.zh: 为什么她会被视为危险人物？

sentences.en: So, Nicolette is not a kind of traditional security threat.
sentences.zh: 尼科莱特并不是那种传统的安全威胁。

sentences.en: She is a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 她是一名律师。

sentences.en: And she didn't know it when she was stopped.
sentences.zh: 她被拦下时并不知情。

sentences.en: But she was caught up in this fight that was happening between the company that operates
sentences.zh: 但她被卷入了运营麦迪逊广场花园的公司与她所在律师事务所之间的纠纷中。

sentences.en: Madison Square Garden and her law firm.
sentences.zh: 她的律所正在代理一起针对麦迪逊广场花园旗下某餐厅的人身伤害诉讼。

sentences.en: Her firm was representing an individual in a personal injury lawsuit against one of Madison
sentences.zh: 而尼科莱特本人根本没有参与这起诉讼。

sentences.en: Square Garden's restaurants.
sentences.zh: 但她确实在那家律所工作。

sentences.en: And Nicolette is not involved in this lawsuit at all.
sentences.zh: 关于麦迪逊广场花园，除了它是世界上最著名的竞技场之一外，还有一点需要了解。

sentences.en: But she does work at the firm.
sentences.zh: 任何对工作人员和粉丝不尊重的人，都会被驱逐并列入黑名单。

sentences.en: And the thing to know about Madison Square Garden, beyond the fact that it's just one of the most famous arenas in the world.
sentences.zh: 那就是拥有它的公司是由亿万富翁詹姆斯·多兰经营的。

sentences.en: So, anybody who comes to the Garden disrespectful to the staff and the fans, they're going to be ejected and they're going to be banned.
sentences.zh: 你不想再来看比赛了是吗？

sentences.en: Is that the company that owns it is run by this billionaire, James Dolan.
sentences.zh: 他以脾气暴躁而闻名。

sentences.en: You want to not come to any more games?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Who is kind of famously temperamental.
sentences.zh: 在电视上看比赛吧。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 他有这样的前科。

sentences.en: Enjoy watching them on TV.
sentences.zh: 卖掉球队！

sentences.en: Has a history of these.
sentences.zh: 你觉得我应该卖掉球队吗？

sentences.en: Sell the team!
sentences.zh: 他与自己拥有的球队——尼克斯队的粉丝有过公开的争执。

sentences.en: Are you thinking I should sell the team?
sentences.zh: 他过去曾禁止过粉丝入场。

sentences.en: Public feuds with fans of the team he owns, the Knicks.
sentences.zh: 大家都在看那边。

sentences.en: He has banned fans in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 显然查尔斯·奥克利在那边。

sentences.en: Everybody looking over there.
sentences.zh: 在看台上打架。

sentences.en: Apparently there's a Charles Oakley over there.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·多兰今天禁止查尔斯·奥克利进入麦迪逊广场花园。

sentences.en: Fighting the stands.
sentences.zh: 你简直不敢相信这是真的。

sentences.en: Jim Dolan today banned Charles Oakley from Madison Square Garden.
sentences.zh: 包括查尔斯·奥克利，这位著名的前尼克斯球员。

sentences.en: You can't make this up.
sentences.zh: 尼克斯队声称奥克利在对尼克斯老板詹姆斯·多兰发表负面评论后被驱逐。

sentences.en: Including Charles Oakley, this famous past Knicks player.
sentences.zh: 他禁止查尔斯·奥克利进入麦迪逊广场花园。

sentences.en: The Knicks claim Oakley was ejected after making negative comments to Knicks owner James Dolan.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯根本就不该坐到他的座位上。

sentences.en: He banned Charles Oakley from Madison Square Garden.
sentences.zh: 我们正在采取措施补救，确保这种情况不会再发生在任何人身上。

sentences.en: Charles never should have made it to his seats.
sentences.zh: 他把这些事情看得非常个人化。

sentences.en: And we're doing things to remedy that, to make sure that that doesn't happen again with anybody.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He takes these things very personally.
sentences.zh: 他很享受这种私人恩怨。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Relishes a good personal battle.
sentences.zh: 因此，麦迪逊广场花园向目前有诉讼案件针对它的约90家律师事务所发出了信函，称这些律所的律师不欢迎进入该公司的场馆。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 即使该律师并未参与针对麦迪逊广场花园或其关联公司的诉讼，

sentences.en: And so Madison Square Garden sent letters to the 90 or so law firms that currently have lawsuits against it and said the lawyers at their firms are not welcome at the company's venues.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是在这些律所工作，就足以让你被禁止进入该场馆。

sentences.en: Even if the lawyer is not involved in litigation against Madison Square Garden or any of the companies associated with it,
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: just working for one of these law firms is enough to get you banned from the venue.
sentences.zh: 据公司官员称，其理由是这些律师可能会以不正当的方式为诉讼收集证据。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 但这些律师表示，这显然是为了阻止他们提起未来的任何诉讼。

sentences.en: And the justification, according to the company's officials, is that those lawyers might be gathering evidence for their lawsuits in an inappropriate way.
sentences.zh: 这真的只是——这是一种报复。

sentences.en: But these lawyers say that this is just clearly a way of discouraging them from filing any future lawsuits.
sentences.zh: 这是企业报复。

sentences.en: And that is really just – it's revenge.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It's corporate revenge.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来确实是对这项技术——人脸识别软件，以及黑名单制度——非常不寻常的使用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种不同寻常的做法。

sentences.en: I mean, this does seem to be a pretty unusual use of this technology, the facial recognition software, as well as blacklists in general.
sentences.zh: 甚至连律师们都说这是一种非常有“创意”的禁令。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is an unusual practice.
sentences.zh: 而且这只有在人脸识别技术的支持下才可能实现。

sentences.en: I mean, even the lawyers have said it's a very creative ban.
sentences.zh: 你知道，否则的话，当有人走进门时，你根本无法分辨他们的雇主是谁。

sentences.en: And it's only possible because of facial recognition technology.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，麦迪逊广场花园拥有这些律所的名单以及在这些律所工作的数千名律师的资料。

sentences.en: You know, it would not – otherwise, you wouldn't be able to tell when somebody walks through the door who their employer was.
sentences.zh: 他们能够从律所自己的网站上获取照片，然后在他们走进门时认出他们。

sentences.en: But in this case, Madison Square Garden has this list of firms and thousands of lawyers that work for the firMs.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一种非常现代且极具未来感的应用。

sentences.en: And they're able to get their photos off their firm's own websites and then spot them as they walk through the door.
sentences.zh: 一些律师称之为“反乌托邦”。

sentences.en: It is very much a modern and really futuristic application of this technology.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为我试着想象一个保安，甚至数百个保安试图做人脸识别软件所做的事情，

sentences.en: Dystopian is what some lawyers have called it.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法想象。

sentences.en: Right, because I'm just trying to imagine a security guard or even hundreds of security guards trying to do what this facial recognition software does,
sentences.zh: 人们肯定会溜进去的。

sentences.en: and you just can't fathom it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，他们可能可以阻止他们买票，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, people would slip through.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们可以把他们的名字列入名单，确保他们买不到票。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, they could likely keep them from buying tickets, right?
sentences.zh: 但要阻止他们让朋友代买门票，这只能通过人脸监控名单来实现。

sentences.en: Like, they could have their name on the list, make sure they don't buy the tickets.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象设计这种强大软件的人初衷是这样的，对吧？把它当作一种将公司的“敌人”拒之门外的方式。

sentences.en: But to be able to prevent them from having friends buy them tickets, this they can only do with a face watch liSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，当我和人脸识别供应商交谈时，他们说，你知道，这是为了安全目的，这是为了保护人们的安全，

sentences.en: I can't imagine this is how the people who designed this very powerful software intended it to be used, right, as a way to keep out a company's enemies from a concert hall.
sentences.zh: 或者它可以以客户服务的方式使用，通过名字来问候人们。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, when I've talked to facial recognition vendors, they've said, you know, this is for security purposes, this is to keep people safe,
sentences.zh: 这不是供应商谈论过的用例。

sentences.en: or it can be used in a customer service kind of way to greet people by name.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我很惊讶看到一家公司这样做，因为它太离谱了。

sentences.en: This is not a use case that vendors have talked about.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人脸识别本身就是一种有争议的技术，以这种方式使用它确实是在挑战底线。

sentences.en: And honestly, I was very surprised to see a company doing this because it is so far out there.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶看到一家公司这样做，而且对自己的所作所为如此直言不讳。

sentences.en: I mean, facial recognition is already a kind of controversial technology, and to wield it in this way is really boundary pushing.
sentences.zh: 当然，问题在于，这合法吗？

sentences.en: And I was surprised to see a company doing it and being so forthright about what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你要与一群律师开战，你应该做好准备，让他们用法律来回击你。

sentences.en: And the question, of course, is, is it legal?
sentences.zh: 这就是正在发生的事情吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, if you're going to go to battle against a bunch of lawyers, you should be prepared for them to throw the law back at you.
sentences.zh: 这就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And is that what's happening?
sentences.zh: 律师们正在起诉麦迪逊广场花园，这些案件正在司法系统中推进。

sentences.en: That is what's happening.
sentences.zh: 而这件事的结果将对未来这项技术的使用方式产生重大影响。

sentences.en: The lawyers are suing Madison Square Garden, and those cases are just making their way through the court system.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实是一个非常不寻常的案例。

sentences.en: And how this turns out is going to have big implications for how the technology gets used in the future.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能让你免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你可以在该应用中免费使用一个月。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 这一个月你可以越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Cashmer, what does the law actually say about when facial recognition technology can and can't be used?
sentences.zh: 卡什米尔，关于人脸识别技术在何时可以使用、何时不能使用，法律到底是怎么说的？

sentences.en: And I should say, we have talked with you a lot on the show about how when it comes to technology, the law tends to lag pretty far behind the technology itself.
sentences.zh: 我得说，我们在节目中和你讨论过很多次，当涉及到技术时，法律往往远远滞后于技术本身。

sentences.en: So, yeah, when it comes to federal law, there is still nothing that really directly applies to facial recognition technology.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在联邦法律方面，目前还没有真正直接适用于人脸识别技术的规定。

sentences.en: So we can set that aside and just look at state laws.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以先撇开这一点，只看州法律。

sentences.en: So Illinois and Texas are the two states that have biometric privacy laws that say you're not supposed to use facial recognition technology without the consent of the person whose face information you're using.
sentences.zh: 伊利诺伊州和德克萨斯州是仅有的两个拥有生物识别隐私法的州，这些法律规定，未经人脸信息被使用者的同意，不得使用人脸识别技术。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So what happened at Madison Square Garden in New York, it sounds like, would not be legal in Texas or Illinois unless the venues had sought permission from someone like Nicolette.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来，在纽约麦迪逊广场花园发生的事情，在德克萨斯州或伊利诺伊州是不合法的，除非场馆方事先征得了像妮可莱特这样的人的许可。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Madison Square Garden actually owns a theater in Illinois, the Chicago Theater.
sentences.zh: 而且麦迪逊广场花园在伊利诺伊州确实拥有一家剧院，即芝加哥剧院。

sentences.en: And the ban applies to that theater, but they are not using facial recognition there to enforce it.
sentences.zh: 禁令适用于那家剧院，但他们并没有在那里使用人脸识别技术来执行禁令。

sentences.en: Ah, how fascinating.
sentences.zh: 啊，真有意思。

sentences.en: So that theater can ban all the lawyers it wants, but it will not have the assistance of this technology.
sentences.zh: 所以那家剧院可以禁止它想禁止的所有律师入内，但它无法借助这项技术来实现。

sentences.en: And what about New York where this behavior occurred and where I assume many of these lawyers have filed their lawsuits?
sentences.zh: 那么在发生这种行为的纽约呢？我假设许多律师已经在那里提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: So when it comes to technology, New York only has a fairly new biometric identifier law that says that if you're a company using it, you need to tell people.
sentences.zh: 当涉及到技术时，纽约只有一项相当新的生物识别标识符法律，规定如果公司在使用该技术，必须告知民众。

sentences.en: There needs to be a sign basically saying facial recognition technology used here.
sentences.zh: 基本上需要立一块牌子，写明此处使用人脸识别技术。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That's not the same as asking people for permission to use it.
sentences.zh: 这和请求人们许可使用是不一样的。

sentences.en: That may mean just putting up a little sign somewhere in the vast hallways of Madison Square Garden saying, P.S., we're using facial recognition technology.
sentences.zh: 这可能仅仅意味着在麦迪逊广场花园宽阔的走廊里随便立个小牌子，写着：顺便提一下，我们正在使用人脸识别技术。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And you have to say why you're using it.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须说明使用它的原因。

sentences.en: And so they do have signs at their venues that say facial recognition technology used here to ensure your safety.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的场馆确实有告示牌，写着“此处使用人脸识别技术以确保您的安全”。

sentences.en: Well, given that fact, what are the lawyers arguing in their lawsuits against Madison Square Garden?
sentences.zh: 那么，鉴于这一事实，律师们在针对麦迪逊广场花园的诉讼中提出了什么论点？

sentences.en: What's the case they're making that what happened to them is improper?
sentences.zh: 他们认为发生在自己身上的事情是不正当的，依据是什么？

sentences.en: So the lawyers found this obscure law from 1941.
sentences.zh: 律师们找到了1941年的一项冷门法律。

sentences.en: It's a New York civil rights law, and it prohibits wrongful refusal of admission to places of public entertainment and amusement.
sentences.zh: 这是纽约的一项民权法，它禁止对公共娱乐和消遣场所进行不正当的拒绝入场。

sentences.en: And that specifically is theaters, music halls, opera houses, and circuses, which I guess were big in the 40s.
sentences.zh: 具体指的就是剧院、音乐厅、歌剧院和马戏团，我想这些在40年代很流行。

sentences.en: So they're focused not on facial recognition technology, but on the idea that they were wrongfully excluded from this venue.
sentences.zh: 所以他们关注的不是人脸识别技术，而是他们被不正当地排除在场馆之外这一事实。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this law has a fascinating history.
sentences.zh: 而且这项法律有着迷人的历史。

sentences.en: It came about because in the early 1900s, theater owners were banning dramatic critics, and it was a way to say, okay, if you give us a bad review, you can't come back.
sentences.zh: 它的出台是因为在20世纪初，剧院老板们开始封杀戏剧评论家，这是一种手段，意思是：好吧，如果你给我们差评，你就别想再来了。

sentences.en: And in the late 1930s, they banned this columnist for the New York Post named Leonard Lyons,
sentences.zh: 在20世纪30年代末，他们封杀了一位《纽约邮报》的专栏作家，名叫伦纳德·莱昂斯，

sentences.en: because he was essentially writing kind of nasty gossip about the Schubert's who owned a bunch of theaters in New York City.
sentences.zh: 因为他基本上是在写关于舒伯特家族的刻薄八卦，而舒伯特家族在纽约市拥有多家剧院。

sentences.en: So he was banned from 30 theaters, and he consulted an ACLU attorney who said, there's not much you can do about it unless you change the law.
sentences.zh: 所以他被30家剧院封杀了，他咨询了一位美国公民自由联盟的律师，对方说，除非你修改法律，否则你对此无能为力。

sentences.en: And so this columnist for the New York Post basically lobbied to get this law passed, and it worked.
sentences.zh: 于是这位《纽约邮报》的专栏作家基本上是通过游说促成了这项法律的通过，而且成功了。

sentences.en: So how do these lawyers say that that law, which clearly seems designed to protect journalists and critics from exclusion, how does it apply to them here?
sentences.zh: 那么这些律师是如何论证这项显然旨在保护记者和评论家免受排斥的法律，适用于他们现在的情况的呢？

sentences.en: So these lawyers say they're exactly like these critics in the early 1900s who were banned because the theater owners essentially didn't like them, and that this law says, hey,
sentences.zh: 这些律师说，他们和20世纪初那些被封杀的评论家完全一样，因为剧院老板本质上不喜欢他们，而这项法律说，嘿，

sentences.en: that doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 那并不重要。

sentences.en: If somebody shows up with a ticket and they're not guilty of abusive behavior or offensive behavior, you have to let them in.
sentences.zh: 如果有人拿着票出现，且没有犯下辱骂或冒犯行为，你就必须让他们进去。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So let's say that these lawyers prevail, that they prove that New York's decades-old anti-discrimination law was violated in this case.
sentences.zh: 假设这些律师胜诉了，证明了纽约这项几十年前的反歧视法在此案中被违反了。

sentences.en: How does that affect the use of facial recognition technology?
sentences.zh: 这会如何影响人脸识别技术的使用？

sentences.en: Because this legal case is, as you said, about an exclusionary blacklist, not about how this technology was used.
sentences.zh: 因为正如你所说，这个法律案件是关于排他性的黑名单，而不是关于这项技术是如何被使用的。

sentences.en: So if they're able to get the ban lifted, it works to attack the facial recognition technology,
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们能解除禁令，这就能起到打击人脸识别技术的作用，

sentences.en: because the facial recognition technology is the only feasible way to do a ban like this.
sentences.zh: 因为人脸识别技术是执行此类禁令唯一可行的方法。

sentences.en: So there's no law they can use to say, hey, this is a horrible use of my face.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有法律依据可以说，嘿，这是对我面部信息的糟糕使用。

sentences.en: But they can use this 1941 law to kind of attack facial recognition from the side.
sentences.zh: 但他们可以利用这项1941年的法律，从侧面打击人脸识别。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In other words, if they prove that the blacklist is illegal,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果他们证明了黑名单是非法的，

sentences.en: then they are simultaneously making it impossible for facial recognition technology to be used to enforce the blackliSt.
sentences.zh: 那么他们同时也使得人脸识别技术无法被用于执行该黑名单。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So how is their case going so far?
sentences.zh: 那么他们的案子目前进展如何？

sentences.en: So a judge has indicated that he agrees with the lawyer's interpretation of this 1941 law and has temporarily lifted the Madison Square Garden ban.
sentences.zh: 一位法官已经表示，他同意律师对这项1941年法律的解读，并暂时解除了麦迪逊广场花园的禁令。

sentences.en: And these lawyers can't buy tickets.
sentences.zh: 而这些律师还是买不到票。

sentences.en: Madison Square Garden doesn't have to sell them tickets.
sentences.zh: 麦迪逊广场花园不必向他们出售门票。

sentences.en: But if they manage to get tickets somehow and they show up at the door wanting to go to a concert or a show, Madison Square Garden does have to let them in.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们设法弄到了票，并且出现在门口想去看音乐会或演出，麦迪逊广场花园确实必须让他们进去。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if Nicolette can get a ticket to a Mariah Carey concert, for example, then Madison Square Garden has to let her in under this injunction.
sentences.zh: 所以如果妮可莱特能弄到一张玛丽亚·凯莉演唱会的门票，那么根据这项禁令，麦迪逊广场花园必须让她进去。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Nicolette's firm is one of the ones that has sued and gotten this injunction.
sentences.zh: 妮可莱特的律所是提起诉讼并获得这项禁令的律所之一。

sentences.en: But a firm does have to sue to actually have a judge grant this to them.
sentences.zh: 但律所确实必须提起诉讼，法官才会批准这一禁令。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So this is a victory.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场胜利。

sentences.en: It is a modest victory.
sentences.zh: 这是一场小小的胜利。

sentences.en: But the 1941 law doesn't mention sporting events.
sentences.zh: 但1941年的法律并没有提到体育赛事。

sentences.en: So these lawyers still can't go to Rangers and Knicks games, which is disappointing.
sentences.zh: 所以这些律师仍然不能去看游骑兵队和尼克斯队的比赛，这很令人失望。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And after that, the judge granted the first injunction for one of the firms that had sued.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，法官为其中一家提起诉讼的律所颁发了第一道禁令。

sentences.en: Benjamin Noren?
sentences.zh: 本杰明·诺伦？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do you work for...
sentences.zh: 你是在为……工作吗？

sentences.en: One of their employment lawyers named Benjamin Noren went to Madison Square Garden to test it.
sentences.zh: 他们的一位劳动法律师本杰明·诺伦去了麦迪逊广场花园进行测试。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I received a order from the Honorable Lyle Frank, which has my name.
sentences.zh: 我收到了莱尔·弗兰克法官的一份命令，上面有我的名字。

sentences.en: He had the order from the judge printed out with him.
sentences.zh: 他把法官打印出来的命令带在身上。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And he walks through the metal detector and he gets pulled aside.
sentences.zh: 他走过金属探测器时被拦了下来。

sentences.en: Come up on a fit and matching somebody on a facial recognition liSt.
sentences.zh: 因为系统显示他与人脸识别名单上的某人匹配。

sentences.en: They used facial recognition technology to identify him.
sentences.zh: 他们使用了人脸识别技术来识别他。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And they said, no, you cannot come in.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，你不能进来。

sentences.en: We are revoking your ticket and you can't go to this concert tonight.
sentences.zh: 我们正在撤销你的门票，你今晚不能参加这场音乐会。

sentences.en: So you're ignoring the court's order.
sentences.zh: 所以你们无视了法院的命令。

sentences.en: No, I believe we are complying with the court's order because we revoked your ticket.
sentences.zh: 不，我相信我们遵守了法院的命令，因为我们撤销了你的门票。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So Madison Square Garden playing a little bit of hardball here, even after the judge files this injunction.
sentences.zh: 所以麦迪逊广场花园在这里表现得有些强硬，即使在法官发布了这项禁令之后。

sentences.en: Yeah, they don't like this judge's decision.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们不喜欢这位法官的裁决。

sentences.en: They don't like a judge telling them who they have to let into their arena.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢法官告诉他们必须让谁进入他们的场馆。

sentences.en: And so they're continuing to fight it in the cases now in appeals court.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在继续抗争，案件目前在上诉法院。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: But it would seem that the judge's decision to file this injunction suggests that he might be leaning towards ruling in favor of these lawyers when it comes to their overall case.
sentences.zh: 但法官决定发布这项禁令，似乎表明他在处理整体案件时，可能倾向于支持这些律师。

sentences.en: Is that how they are seeing it?
sentences.zh: 他们是这样看的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the lawyers see this as a very good sign for them.
sentences.zh: 是的，律师们认为这是一个非常好的迹象。

sentences.en: But, you know, this is not the end of the case.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这还不是案件的终结。

sentences.en: This is not the resolution.
sentences.zh: 这还不是最终结果。

sentences.en: This still could turn out in favor of Madison Square Garden.
sentences.zh: 事情仍有可能对麦迪逊广场花园有利。

sentences.en: And if so, that would be, you know, kind of an implicit endorsement of how they're using the technology.
sentences.zh: 如果是那样的话，那将是对他们使用该技术方式的一种隐性认可。

sentences.en: And it would set a precedent for other businesses to use it in a similar way.
sentences.zh: 并且会为其他企业以类似方式使用该技术开创先例。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It seems that the approach these lawyers are taking, which is the legal route, makes sense because they're lawyers.
sentences.zh: 这些律师采取的方法，即法律途径，似乎是合理的，因为他们是律师。

sentences.en: But for everybody else, isn't the better solution having states regulate facial recognition technology the way that Illinois and Texas have?
sentences.zh: 但对于其他人来说，更好的解决方案难道不是让各州像伊利诺伊州和德克萨斯州那样监管人脸识别技术吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that potentially the easiest route for making sure that we have actual guidelines around how this technology is used and so that you don't end up on a facial recognition technology enemies list at your local theater?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是确保我们有关于如何使用该技术的实际准则，从而让你不会出现在当地剧院的人脸识别黑名单上的最简单途径吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, this case is exactly the kind of scenario that privacy advocates have been talking to me about, you know, hypothetically, theoretically, what was possible.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这个案件正是隐私倡导者一直跟我谈论的那种情况，你知道，假设性的、理论上的可能性。

sentences.en: They really don't think that companies should have this power to discriminate between the customers who walk through their door and immediately know, yeah,
sentences.zh: 他们真的认为公司不应该拥有这种权力，去歧视走进门的顾客，并立即知道，是的，

sentences.en: who they work for or what their ideology is because it really opens the door for all kinds of different discrimination.
sentences.zh: 他们为谁工作或他们的意识形态是什么，因为这确实为各种各样的歧视打开了大门。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And it seems like they fear that in the absence of this kind of regulation, we're going to see this technology used more widely in exactly this kind of manner as a tool, basically,
sentences.zh: 而且看起来他们担心，在缺乏这种监管的情况下，我们将看到这项技术以这种方式被更广泛地使用，基本上作为一种工具，

sentences.en: of revenge rather than security.
sentences.zh: 一种报复工具，而不是安全工具。

sentences.en: Yeah, they think that it needs to be regulated or even, you know, some say that facial recognition technology should be banned entirely.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们认为它需要被监管，甚至有人说应该完全禁止人脸识别技术。

sentences.en: And, you know, their fear is, if it's not, there's going to be all kinds of different watch lists.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们的恐惧是，如果不禁止，将会出现各种各样的观察名单。

sentences.en: And the lawyers themselves I've talked to, I mean, they're pretty aware they're not the most sympathetic victiMs.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的律师们，他们很清楚自己不是最令人同情的受害者。

sentences.en: But they're saying, hey, we're the canary in the coal mine here.
sentences.zh: 但他们说，嘿，我们是这里的煤矿金丝雀。

sentences.en: Businesses are run by people and people have all kinds of different reasons to dislike potential customers.
sentences.zh: 企业是由人经营的，而人有各种各样的理由去讨厌潜在的顾客。

sentences.en: You could just imagine watch lists that were based on your politics.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一下基于你的政治立场而建立的观察名单。

sentences.en: You might criticize a business on Yelp, you know, leave them a nasty review, and then you discover you're never allowed to go inside again.
sentences.zh: 你可能会在Yelp上批评一家企业，给他们留下差评，然后你发现自己再也不被允许进入了。

sentences.en: Businesses do get to decide in many ways who they do business with.
sentences.zh: 企业在很多方面确实有权决定与谁做生意。

sentences.en: And so we may just find that we can't shop at certain places, and you may not even know why.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会发现自己无法在某些地方消费，而且你甚至可能不知道原因。

sentences.en: You just walk in, your face sets up an alert in the system, and they say you're not welcome here.
sentences.zh: 你只是走进去，你的脸在系统中触发了警报，然后他们说你不受欢迎。

sentences.en: So this might sound theoretical, it might sound dystopian, like something from science fiction.
sentences.zh: 所以这听起来可能是理论上的，听起来可能是反乌托邦的，就像科幻小说里的东西。

sentences.en: But with Madison Square Garden, we've seen not only is it technologically possible, it is happening.
sentences.zh: 但对于麦迪逊广场花园，我们已经看到，这不仅在技术上是可能的，而且正在发生。

sentences.en: Well, Kashmir, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，卡什米尔，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: For the first time in decades, China's population has begun to shrink.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，中国人口首次开始萎缩。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, the government said that over the past year, deaths had outnumbered births by nearly a million, a demographic crisis that China has long sought to avoid.
sentences.zh: 周二，政府表示，在过去的一年中，死亡人数比出生人数多出近一百万，这是中国长期以来一直试图避免的人口危机。

sentences.en: Researchers say that unless China can reverse its declining birth rate, it may not have enough people of working age to fuel its growth.
sentences.zh: 研究人员表示，除非中国能够扭转出生率下降的趋势，否则可能没有足够的劳动年龄人口来推动其增长。

sentences.en: And police in New Mexico have arrested a former Republican candidate for state legislature for allegedly paying gunmen to shoot at the homes of four local Democratic officials.
sentences.zh: 新墨西哥州警方逮捕了一名前共和党州议会候选人，指控他花钱雇佣枪手向四名当地民主党官员的家中开枪。

sentences.en: The candidate, Solomon Pena, lost his election by a landslide in November and approached several Democratic officials with claims that the race had been rigged.
sentences.zh: 这名候选人所罗门·佩尼亚在11月的选举中惨败，并曾向几位民主党官员声称选举被操纵了。

sentences.en: After some of the officials rejected his claims, police say he conspired to attack their houses.
sentences.zh: 在一些官员拒绝了他的说法后，警方称他密谋袭击了他们的住所。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Astha Chaturvedi, Will Reed, and Mary Wilson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由阿斯塔·查图尔维迪、威尔·里德和玛丽·威尔逊制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by John Ketchum and Michael Benoit, contains original music by Rowan Emisto and Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Corey Schreppel.
sentences.zh: 由约翰·凯彻姆和迈克尔·贝努瓦编辑，包含罗文·埃米斯托和马里昂·洛萨诺的原创音乐，并由科里·施雷佩尔进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争中。
